note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), original in English; the original combination is Termes convexus Walker, 1853, now placed in Kalotermes. Measurements in mm. Distribution: Tasmania. The original records a few alates taken on 12 February (month 2) from a wood heap at the Macquarie River and at Hobart, and supposes the species to be common in the forest. Type material: the alate holotype is in the British Museum. Taxonomic doubt: Hagen (1858) merged T. obscurus Walker from Western Australia into this species and described "soldier and worker"; Hill pointed out that the two are not the same species; Holmgren considered that the soldiers and workers recorded by Froggatt as C. convexus are in fact Porotermes froggatti, and Hill considered that the soldiers recorded by Hagen are very probably P. froggatti. OCR problems: the genus name mostly appears as oonvexas / conveccus; the braces in "Calotermes {Cryptotermes ?) conveccus" are misrecognised parentheses; the OCR gives the length without wings as "4. l+O—5.75", read as 4.40—5.75 from the digit shapes; "la.hrum" and "Habrum" are misrecognitions of labrum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small, hairless, dark brown species; pronotum slightly darker than the head, anteclypeus whitish, labrum lemon yellow, wings pale brown. Compound eyes small (diameter 0.22 × 0.25). Ocelli small, close to but not touching the compound eyes. Antennae 12—14-segmented. Pronotum (Fig. 52) large, distinctly wider than the head, not distinctly arched, anterior margin strongly concave, sides distinctly widened at the middle, posterior margin wide and rather deeply concave, margins with impressions, with only sparse, very short hairs. Wings pale brown, venation very variable; the subcosta of the fore wing is about as long as the width of the wing at the suture; the radius is about twice as long as the subcosta; the radial sector has about 12 branches; the media runs roughly parallel to the radial sector to the wing apex, closer to the radial sector than to the cubitus, or joins the radial sector before or after the middle of the wing; the cubitus is almost parallel to the media, running slightly above or slightly below the middle of the wing, or joins the radial sector before the wing apex. Tibial spurs without serrations. Measurements (mm): length with wings 8.00; length without wings 4.40—5.75; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.21; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.80—0.91; head width 0.95—1.00; pronotum length 0.58—0.66; pronotum width 1.10—1.13; fore wing length 6.75; fore wing width 1.90.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The original heads this section "Soldier (undescribed)": two unidentified Calotermes soldiers have been collected in Tasmania, and it cannot at present be decided whether either of them belongs to this species, so no soldier description or measurements are given.
